executive_summary: Revenue grew 4.6% to $3,257.5m (FY25: $3,114.6m), driven by Employee Share Plans (+18.0% reported, +10.2% CC), Corporate Trust (+9.6% reported, +5.7% CC) and Issuer Services (+7.7% reported, +4.4% CC); FX tailwinds added $53.2m. Statutory NPAT rose only 1.9% to $618.7m due to the $78.3m gross cost of the UK Mortgage Services disposal (loss $46.3m + disposal-related costs $32.0m) and a 360bp jump in effective tax rate to 27.0% from 23.4%. Management NPAT (underlying) rose 7.3% to $849.8m (Management EPS 146.92 cps vs. 135.28 cps).

The single most important issue for investors is the trajectory of Margin Income: MI fell $5.5m (-0.7%) to $755.6m as rate cuts across all major markets (-63bps weighted avg yield to 2.36%) were almost entirely offset by average client balance growth of $2.1bn to $32.0bn. The hedge book (WAL 5.07 years) locks in ~$1.9bn of MI over FY26-FY35, providing structural earnings resilience. FY27 guidance for MI of ~$770m implies a recovery driven by balance growth and hedging, even as rates are assumed flat. Net debt collapsed to $144.1m (0.11x EBITDA) from $527.6m, the balance sheet now almost unleveraged.

Red flag — the statutory effective tax rate surged to 27.0% (FY25: 23.4%), adding ~$43.6m in tax versus a stable-rate scenario; the UK MS disposal generated $19.5m of non-deductible losses under UK Substantial Shareholding Exemption rules (gain is exempt but loss is also not deductible, creating a permanent difference), and the prior period benefited from a one-off US state tax methodology change ($16.3m prior-year over-provision credit). Restructuring costs remain persistent at $61.6m after-tax for the 6th consecutive year, and Technology & Operations absorbed $97.9m management EBIT loss (excluding stranded costs) — the corporate cost sink is not shrinking. Additionally, Issuer Services management EBIT ex-MI fell 4.6% CC to $209.2m as newly acquired businesses diluted margins and stranded costs were reallocated.

key_numbers.revenue: $3,257.5m vs. $3,114.6m (PCP), up 4.6%; organic CC growth ~3.0% excluding FX and portfolio changes
key_numbers.ebitda_margin: Management EBITDA $1,284.9m (actual FX); statutory EBITDA not explicitly disclosed but implied ~$1,023m pre-finance costs and tax. Management EBITDA margin 39.3% of management revenue vs. 39.9% PCP (per segment data). Operating cash to EBITDA conversion 65% (stable vs. 66% PCP)
key_numbers.npat_underlying: Management NPAT $849.8m vs. $793.8m (PCP), up 7.0%. Difference of $231.1m (after-tax) comprises: amortisation of acquisition intangibles $76.3m, acquisitions/disposals $84.9m (UK MS loss $46.3m + disposal costs $32.0m + other), restructuring $61.6m, hedge modification $8.6m and other. These items have recurred for multiple years, making 'underlying' a generous label for persistently recurring costs
key_numbers.eps: Basic statutory EPS 106.97 cps vs. 103.45 cps (PCP), up 3.4%. Management EPS 146.92 cps vs. 135.28 cps (PCP), up 8.6% (at reported WANOS of 578.4m)
key_numbers.operating_cashflow: $836.6m vs. $823.7m (PCP), up 1.6%; cash conversion to management EBITDA 65% vs. 66% PCP; impacted by $53.0m receivables outflow and higher prepayments (long-term tech contracts)
key_numbers.free_cashflow: $801.2m vs. $780.1m (PCP), up 2.7% (defined as operating cash less capex of $35.4m; no capitalised development costs — software expensed)
key_numbers.net_debt_cash: Net debt $144.1m at 30 June 2026 vs. $527.6m at 30 June 2025; reduction of $383.5m driven by strong FCF and $562.8m net debt repayment; leverage 0.11x EBITDA vs. 0.42x. Total borrowings $1,197.8m non-current, nil current; cash $1,053.7m

analysis.quality_of_earnings: Cash conversion is healthy at 65% of management EBITDA but has edged down from 66% in FY25, partly due to a $53m receivables build and $24.7m in non-current prepayments for long-term technology contracts (a form of off-balance-sheet capex deferral). Receivables rose $19.9m to $566.8m. No material development costs are capitalised (explicitly confirmed), which is a positive quality signal. However, management adjustment items have now totalled $231.1m (FY26), $186.8m (FY25), and $355.7m (FY24) — over $770m across three years — with restructuring costs ($61.6m net of tax in FY26) recurring for the 6th consecutive year and integration charges ($10.8m) still flowing through despite major acquisitions being largely complete. The $8.6m non-cash hedge modification charge (unwinding through FY34) obscures true interest economics. Statutory ETR of 27.0% versus management ETR of 24.6% also flags non-recurring distortions that inflate the gap between statutory and underlying profit.
analysis.management_framing: Mixed — the presentation leads strongly with management (non-IFRS) metrics: Management EPS 145.2 cps (CC) / 146.92 cps (actual) is the headline number, while statutory EPS of 106.97 cps and NPAT growth of just 1.9% are disclosed only in the appendix. The deck emphasises the 35.4% final dividend increase and 58% payout ratio, ROIC of 36.5%, near-zero leverage, and 10.4% CAGR in management EPS since FY23 — all legitimate positives. Downplayed: the UK MS disposal destroyed $46.3m of value (sold for $13.0m net against $34.2m net assets plus $15.2m FX reserve reclassification plus $9.9m transaction costs), Issuer Services EBIT ex-MI fell 4.6% in CC terms, the effective tax rate step-up, and the Technology & Operations segment running a -$97.9m management EBIT loss (including stranded costs). The segment reclassification — combining four sub-segments into 'Corporate & Other' — reduces visibility into stranded cost progress going forward. Management explicitly note this will be the 'final year' of cost-out reporting, which removes a key tracking mechanism for investors.
positives: Employee Share Plans delivered standout performance: revenue +10.2% CC to $559.7m, management EBIT +24.3% to $260.8m, EBIT margin expanded 530bps to 46.6%, and EBIT ex-MI margin up 710bps to 42.0% CC — driven by transactional revenue +18.6% to $316.9m and AuA of $288.6bn (+8%). This is a high-quality, recurring-revenue growth business benefiting from structural trend of equity-based remuneration.

Balance sheet transformation: net debt fell to $144.1m (0.11x EBITDA) from $527.6m (0.42x), EBITDA interest coverage rose to 15.6x from 10.7x, average cost of debt declined 122bps to 5.53%, and $1,083m of undrawn bank facilities remain available. Free cash flow of $801.2m supports 55% dividend payout ratio (up from 45%) and positions the company for acquisitions. FY27 interest expense is guided down ~15%, adding ~2 cps to management EPS.

Margin Income structural protection: $1.9bn of hedged MI locked in over FY26-FY35 (WAL 5.07 years), with exposed balances up $1.3bn to $10.0bn and recapture rate improving to 97%. The hedge book's growing contribution ($331.6m in FY26 vs. $314.9m FY25) increasingly offsets rate cuts, and FY27 MI is guided to ~$770m — a recovery from FY26 — as hedged balances rise from $9.6bn to $11.7bn at yield of 3.64%.

Corporate Trust synergies ahead of schedule: $80m Wells Fargo synergies delivered one year early; cumulative CCT synergies of $83.4m (cost $29.7m + revenue $53.7m) against a $116m total plan target, with $5m remaining to be delivered in FY27. Revenue grew 5.7% CC to $1,032.0m with structured products mandates won up 21.9%.
negatives: UK Mortgage Services disposal was value-destructive: sold for $13.0m gross consideration (net cash outflow $3.4m after deducting $9.8m cash disposed) against net assets of $34.2m plus $15.2m FX reserves reclassified, plus $9.9m transaction costs = $46.3m pre-tax loss. Zero tax benefit under UK Substantial Shareholding Exemption. Additionally, $32.0m of redundancy/provisions were charged as disposal-related expenses below the EBIT line. Total cash and P&L cost ~$78.3m gross. This follows a pattern of loss-making disposals (US MS loss $129.4m in FY24).

Effective tax rate jumped 360bps to 27.0% from 23.4%, adding ~$30m+ in tax versus PCP normalized rate; the management ETR of 24.6% is more stable but the statutory gap to prior year reflects $19.5m of permanent differences from UK MS disposal and the absence of the $16.3m prior-year US state tax benefit. FY27 guidance assumes ~24% management ETR but statutory rate uncertainty remains elevated.

Issuer Services EBIT ex-MI fell 4.6% CC to $209.2m (margin down 220bps to 19.3% CC) despite revenue growth of 4.4%, as newly acquired businesses (ingage, CMi2i) dilute margins while scaling, and $13.3m of stranded costs were allocated back. Global managed shareholder accounts continue to shrink (33.9m units in FY26 vs. 35.1m in FY25), indicating structural headwinds in the register maintenance core.

Restructuring and integration costs remain persistently high and are being excluded from 'underlying' earnings: $61.6m major restructuring (after-tax) in FY26 after $60.7m in FY25 and $47.1m in FY24; total cost-to-achieve post-tax of $609.4m cumulative. FY26 is described as the 'final year' of cost-out reporting, removing future accountability. Technology costs rose to 10.9% of revenue ($356m) from 10.2% ($317m), with maintenance +36% to $64.2m, signalling tech debt rather than transformation progress.

bottom_line.bull: CPU is a near-unlevered, cash-generative infrastructure business with a 10.4% management EPS CAGR since FY23, structural MI protection via a $1.9bn hedged book (WAL 5 years), and a powerful growth engine in Employee Share Plans (EBIT margin 46.6% and rising). FY27 management EPS guidance of ~154 cps (+6%) is supported by MI recovery ($770m), lower interest expense (~15% reduction), and EBIT ex-MI expansion to ~19%; the dividend (AUD 120 cps total in FY26 vs. 93 cps FY25) reflects genuine balance sheet strength and management confidence.
bottom_line.bear: Statutory earnings growth is just 1.9% after absorbing recurring 'non-recurring' costs that have totalled $770m+ over three years, ongoing value-destructive disposals, and a structurally rising tax rate. Issuer Services core margins are compressing, managed shareholder accounts are declining, technology costs are inflating, and the Technology & Operations segment absorbs ~$98m annually. MI sensitivity remains: a 100bps rate decline would cost ~$72m in annual MI at current exposed balance levels, and the hedge book yield advantage reverses post-FY31 as older higher-rate swaps mature.
bottom_line.what_changes_mind: Bull-to-bear: a sustained decline in global interest rates below 3% (MI falls to ~$728m at 3% rates per sensitivity table, and lower still if exposed balances soften); failure to deploy the $1bn+ balance sheet firepower on value-accretive acquisitions (risk of returning to low-quality bolt-ons at high prices); or Issuer Services margin recovery stalling as stranded cost reallocation continues. Bear-to-bull: evidence that management EPS ex-MI can reach the 20% margin target (currently 18.1%), demonstrated by Issuer Services ex-MI margin recovering above 21% and restructuring costs finally ceasing (FY28 per guidance); or a large-scale Corporate Trust or Entity Solutions acquisition that immediately accretive at scale.
